scheme_name: Financial Assistance For Education Of Children Of Registered Worker (HBOCWWB)
description:
The Financial Assistance for Education of Children of Registered Workers scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India to support the education of children of registered workers in the construction sector.

This scheme was initiated by the Haryana Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (HBOCWWB) in 2008.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to the children of registered construction workers to ensure that they receive quality education.

The scheme aims to reduce the dropout rates among children of construction workers and encourage them to pursue their studies.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is aimed at students from Class 1 to Class 12.

The assistance amount varies according to the educational level of the child.

For students in Class 1 to Class 5, the scheme provides an annual financial assistance of ₹3,000.

For students in Class 6 to Class 8, the annual assistance increases to ₹4,000.

Students in Class 9 to Class 10 receive an annual financial assistance of ₹5,000.

For students in Class 11 to Class 12, the assistance amount is ₹6,000 per year.

The scheme also aims to promote higher education among the children of construction workers.

For students pursuing technical or professional courses after completing their schooling, the scheme provides financial assistance of ₹10,000 per year.

To be eligible for this scheme, the applicant must be a registered construction worker under the HBOCWWB.

The worker must have been registered for a minimum of one year to qualify for the benefits.

The children of registered workers must be studying in recognized schools or educational institutions.

There are no specific age limits mentioned for the children under this scheme.

However, the educational qualifications must be in line with the class levels for which the assistance is being sought.

The application process for the scheme is straightforward and designed to be user-friendly.

Interested applicants must fill out the application form available on the official HBOCWWB website or at designated offices.

The application form requires details such as the name of the worker, registration number, and details of the child for whom assistance is being requested.

Applicants must also submit proof of the child’s enrollment in a recognized educational institution.

Additionally, a copy of the worker's registration certificate must be attached to the application.

Once the application is completed, it should be submitted to the local HBOCWWB office.

The application can also be submitted online through the official HBOCWWB portal.

The processing time for applications is generally around 30 days from the date of submission.

Disbursement of funds is typically done through direct bank transfers to the accounts of the beneficiaries.

The financial assistance is disbursed annually based on the academic year.

The scheme is implemented by the Haryana Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

The HBOCWWB operates under the Department of Labour and Employment, Government of Haryana.

For any queries or assistance, beneficiaries can contact the HBOCWWB office at their local district headquarters.

The contact details for the HBOCWWB can be found on their official website.

The scheme has been instrumental in improving educational outcomes for children of construction workers in Haryana.

As of 2023, the scheme has benefited thousands of children across the state.

The government has allocated a significant budget for this scheme to ensure its sustainability.

In the financial year 2022-2023, the government allocated ₹50 crores for the welfare of construction workers and their families.

The scheme has also been recognized for its role in promoting social equity and inclusion.

It addresses the financial barriers that often prevent children from low-income families from accessing quality education.

The scheme is part of a broader set of initiatives aimed at improving the living standards of construction workers in Haryana.

The HBOCWWB also offers other welfare measures such as health insurance and housing assistance.

The financial assistance for education is a critical component of the overall welfare strategy for construction workers.

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have reported improved educational performance among their children.

Regular monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted to assess its impact and effectiveness.

The government encourages feedback from beneficiaries to improve the scheme further.

In conclusion, the Financial Assistance for Education of Children of Registered Workers scheme is a vital initiative that supports the educational aspirations of children from low-income families in the construction sector.

It provides substantial financial assistance to ensure that these children can pursue their studies without financial constraints.

The scheme reflects the government's commitment to enhancing educational opportunities for all segments of society.

By focusing on the education of children of registered workers, the scheme aims to break the cycle of poverty and promote upward mobility.

This initiative is a step towards building a more equitable society where every child has the right to education and the opportunity to succeed.
